# Analysis

## Install packages
```{r}
install.packages("lmerTest")
install.packages("performance")
install.packages("emmeans")
install.packages("dplyr")
install.packages("tidyr")
```

## Load packages
```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(performance)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

```

# Load data

```{r}
dat <- read_delim("/Users/vivianhunziker/Desktop/Master Thesis Vivian Hunziker/Data/data_06.10.2026.csv")



# SEX -> MUSS NOCH IM ANDEREN DOK GEMACHT WERDEN...
```

# H1

## H1a: well-being

```{r}
# Filter datased
dat_rq1_wb <- dat %>%
  filter(#!is.na(wellbeing), 
    !is.na(K9_orientation), !is.na(sex), !is.na(ses)) %>%
  mutate(ses_c = (ses - mean(ses[!duplicated(person_id)])) / 10)


# model zero
m0_wb <- lmer(
  wellbeing ~ 1 + (1 | person_id),
  data = dat_rq1_wb,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m0_wb)
icc(m0_wb)

# main model
m3_wb <- lmer(
  wellbeing ~ wave * K9_orientation + sex + ses_c +
    (1 | person_id),
  data = dat_rq1_wb,
  REML = TRUE
)

summary(m3_wb)

confint(m3_wb, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")

# 1. Omnibus tests
anova(m3_wb)

# 2. Estimated marginal means
emm_wb <- emmeans(m3_wb, ~ K9_orientation | wave)
summary(emm_wb, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE))

# 3. Group differences within waves
diff_wb <- pairs(emm_wb)
summary(diff_wb, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE))

# 4. Standardized group differences

 #Extract the existing group contrasts
diff_wb_ci <- as.data.frame(summary(diff_wb, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
 #Calculate the model-implied total standard deviation
vc_wb <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m3_wb))
sd_total_wb <- sqrt(sum(vc_wb$vcov))
# Calculate standardized group differences
diff_wb_ci$d <- diff_wb_ci$estimate / sd_total_wb
# Calculate approximate standardized confidence interval limits
diff_wb_ci$d_low <- diff_wb_ci$asymp.LCL / sd_total_wb
diff_wb_ci$d_up <- diff_wb_ci$asymp.UCL / sd_total_wb

diff_wb_ci

# 5. Changes in group differences across waves
change_wb <- contrast(
  diff_wb,
  method = "revpairwise",
  by = NULL
)
summary(change_wb, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

# 6. Within-group changes across assessment waves

# Estimate well-being at each wave within each orientation group
emm_wb_time <- emmeans(
  m3_wb,
  ~ wave | K9_orientation
)

# Compare waves within each orientation group
time_diff_wb <- pairs(emm_wb_time)

# Display within-group changes and 95% confidence intervals
summary(time_diff_wb, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE))
```

### Plot

```{r}
pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.25)

# Panel A: estimated mean
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_wb)

p_means <- ggplot(
  emm_df,
  aes(x = wave, y = emmean, group = K9_orientation,
      linetype = K9_orientation, shape = K9_orientation)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, position = pd) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, position = pd) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL),
                width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.5,
                linetype = "solid", position = pd) +
  labs(x = "Assessment wave", y = "Estimated well-being",
       linetype = "Sexual orientation", shape = "Sexual orientation") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 9, color = "black"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))

p_means
```

# Model assumptions H1a

```{r}
# 1. Normally Distributed Residuals
#  Level-1: standardised residuals
res_wb <- residuals(m3_wb, scaled = TRUE)

#  Level-2: random intercepts
ri_wb <- ranef(m3_wb)$person_id[, "(Intercept)"]

# Plots two sho Level-1 residuals and random intercepts
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Level-1-residuals
qqnorm(
  res_wb,
  main = "Level-1: Residuen",
  xlab = "Theoretical Quantiles",
  ylab = "Standardized Residuals",
  pch = 1
)
qqline(res_wb, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Level-2: Random Intercepts
qqnorm(
  ri_wb,
  main = "Level-2: Random Intercepts",
  xlab = "Theoretical Quantiles",
  ylab = "Random Intercepts",
  pch = 1
)
qqline(ri_wb, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# set back graphical information
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


# 2. Linearity
# Wave is modeled as a categorical predictor; therefore,no linear time trend is assumed.


# 3. Homoscedascity
# Level-1 residuals per wave

# data for diagnostics
dat_diag <- data.frame(
  residual = residuals(m3_wb),
  wave = model.frame(m3_wb)$wave,
  orientation = model.frame(m3_wb)$K9_orientation
)

ggplot(dat_diag, aes(x = wave, y = residual)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.15, color = "blue") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.4, alpha = 0.2, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Level-1 Residuals by Wave",
    x = "Assessment Wave",
    y = "Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Level-1 residuals by Waxe x Orientation
ggplot(
  dat_diag,
  aes(x = wave, y = residual, fill = orientation)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    alpha = 0.5,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Level-1 Residuals by Wave and Orientation",
    x = "Assessment Wave",
    y = "Residuals",
    fill = "Sexual Attraction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



# 4. Outlier
# Level-1 outlier

# Data out of the estimated model
dat_out_wb <- model.frame(m3_wb) %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted(m3_wb),
    residual = residuals(m3_wb),
    std_residual = residuals(m3_wb, scaled = TRUE)
  )

# number of unusual participants
sum(abs(dat_out_wb$std_residual) > 3)

# show unusual participants 
outliers_L1_wb <- dat_out_wb %>%
  filter(abs(std_residual) > 3) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(std_residual)))

outliers_L1_wb

# Plot: Level-1 outliers
ggplot(dat_out_wb,
       aes(x = fitted, y = std_residual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(
    data = outliers_L1_wb,
    color = "red",
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(-3, 0, 3),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Level-1 Outliers: Well-being",
    x = "Fitted Values",
    y = "Standardized Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



# Level-2 outliers
# extract random intercepts
ri_wb <- ranef(m3_wb)$person_id[, "(Intercept)"]

dat_ri_wb <- data.frame(
  person_id = rownames(ranef(m3_wb)$person_id),
  random_intercept = as.numeric(ri_wb)
) %>%
  mutate(
    z_intercept = as.numeric(scale(random_intercept))
  )

# number of unusual random intercepts
sum(abs(dat_ri_wb$z_intercept) > 3)

# unusual participants
outliers_L2_wb <- dat_ri_wb %>%
  filter(abs(z_intercept) > 3) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(z_intercept)))

outliers_L2_wb

# Plot: level-2 outlier
ggplot(dat_ri_wb,
       aes(x = random_intercept, y = z_intercept)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(
    data = outliers_L2_wb,
    color = "red",
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(-3, 3),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Level-2 Outliers: Random Intercepts",
    x = "Estimated Random Intercept",
    y = "Standardized Random Intercept"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



# individual unusual trajectories ouver time
ids_out_wb <- outliers_L2_wb$person_id

# data out of the estimated model
dat_plot_wb <- model.frame(m3_wb) %>%
  mutate(
    person_id = as.character(person_id),
    outlier = if_else(
      person_id %in% ids_out_wb,
      "Auffälliger Random Intercept",
      "Übrige Personen"
    )
  )

# Plot
ggplot(dat_plot_wb,
       aes(x = wave, y = wellbeing,
           group = person_id)) +
  geom_line(
    data = subset(dat_plot_wb,
                  outlier == "Übrige Personen"),
    color = "grey70",
    alpha = 0.12
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = subset(dat_plot_wb,
                  outlier == "Auffälliger Random Intercept"),
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Individual Well-being Trajectories",
    x = "Assessment Wave",
    y = "Well-being"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()



# 5. Influential Participants
# influence diagnostic on person level
infl_wb <- influence(
  m3_wb,
  group = "person_id"
)

# Calculate Cook's distance for each participant
cooks_wb <- cooks.distance(infl_wb)

# Plot Cook's Distance
plot(
  cooks_wb,
  type = "h",
  main = "Cook's Distance by Participant",
  xlab = "Participant",
  ylab = "Cook's Distance"
)

# 10 biggest values
head(sort(cooks_wb, decreasing = TRUE), 10)



# 6. convergence and singularity
# convergence
check_convergence(m3_wb)

# singularity
check_singularity(m3_wb)
```

# H2a: well-being 

```{r}
# K7 Well-being as baseline for each participant
baseline_wb <- dat %>%
  filter(wave == "K7") %>%
  select(person_id, wellbeing_K7 = wellbeing)

# join 
dat_rq2_wb <- dat %>%
  left_join(baseline_wb, by = "person_id")

nrow(dat_rq2_wb)

# CHECK if a participant needs more than one row
baseline_wb %>% count(person_id) %>% filter(n > 1)

# select complete cases
dat_rq2_wb_k9 <- dat_rq2_wb %>%
  filter(wave == "K9") %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(wellbeing),
    !is.na(wellbeing_K7),
    !is.na(K7_ResilFriends),
    !is.na(K9_orientation),
    !is.na(sex),
    !is.na(ses)) %>%
  mutate(ses_c = (ses - mean(ses[!duplicated(person_id)])) / 10)

table(dat_rq2_wb_k9$K9_orientation)

# center inernalizing and K7_ResilFriends ### -> vielleicht in ein separaten Chunk tun
dat_rq2_wb_k9 <- dat_rq2_wb_k9 %>%
  mutate(
    wb_K7_c = wellbeing_K7 -
      mean(wellbeing_K7, na.rm = TRUE),

    peer_c = K7_ResilFriends -
      mean(K7_ResilFriends, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Base model
model_rq2_wb_base <- lm(
  wellbeing ~ wb_K7_c +
    peer_c + K9_orientation + sex + ses_c,
  data = dat_rq2_wb_k9
)

summary(model_rq2_wb_base)


# Interactionmodel
model_rq2_wb_mod <- lm(
  wellbeing ~ wb_K7_c +
    peer_c * K9_orientation + sex + ses_c,
  data = dat_rq2_wb_k9
)

summary(model_rq2_wb_mod)

# Cohens D 
parameters::standardize_parameters(model_rq2_wb_mod, method = "refit")

# 95%-CI
confint(model_rq2_wb_base)
confint(model_rq2_wb_mod)

# Modellgüte
summary(model_rq2_wb_base)$r.squared
summary(model_rq2_wb_mod)$r.squared

# adjusted R²
summary(model_rq2_wb_base)$adj.r.squared
summary(model_rq2_wb_mod)$adj.r.squared

# additionally explained value 
delta_R2 <-
  summary(model_rq2_wb_mod)$r.squared -
  summary(model_rq2_wb_base)$r.squared

delta_R2
```

## Plot

```{r}
cols <- c("Heterosexual"     = "#D55E00",
          "Non-heterosexual" = "#0072B2")

# Mean value used to center peer_c (data from H2a!)
peer_mean_wb <- mean(dat_rq2_wb_k9$K7_ResilFriends, na.rm = TRUE)
peer_grid_wb <- seq(2.33, 4, length.out = 50)

pred_wb <- emmeans(
  model_rq2_wb_mod,
  ~ K9_orientation | peer_c,
  at = list(peer_c = peer_grid_wb - peer_mean_wb, wb_K7_c = 0)
)
pred_df_wb <- as.data.frame(pred_wb) |>
  mutate(peer = peer_c + peer_mean_wb)

# Number of individuals per measurement value and group (from 2.33 onwards)
obs_wb <- dat_rq2_wb_k9 %>%
  filter(K7_ResilFriends >= 2.33) %>%
  mutate(peer = round(K7_ResilFriends, 2)) %>%
  count(peer, K9_orientation) %>%
  tidyr::complete(peer, K9_orientation, fill = list(n = 0))

# Main plot (full scale 1–4, without x-axis label)
p_main_wb <- ggplot(
  pred_df_wb,
  aes(x = peer, y = emmean, color = K9_orientation,
      fill = K9_orientation, linetype = K9_orientation)
) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), alpha = 0.12, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed")) +
```

### Model assumptions

```{r}
# 1. Normality of Residuals
# Plot standardized residuals
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

qqnorm(
  rstandard(model_rq2_wb_mod),
  main = "Q-Q Plot: Residuals"
)
qqline(rstandard(model_rq2_wb_mod), col = "red")

hist(
  rstandard(model_rq2_wb_mod),
  main = "Distribution of Residuals",
  xlab = "Standardized Residuals"
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


# 2. Linearity
# Check linearity of continuous predictors in the base model
car::crPlots(
  model_rq2_wb_base,
  terms = ~ wb_K7_c + peer_c + ses_c
)


# 3. Homoscedasticity
# Extract fitted values and residuals from the moderation model
dat_diag_rq2_wb <- data.frame(
  fitted = fitted(model_rq2_wb_mod),
  residual = residuals(model_rq2_wb_mod)
)

# Plot residuals against fitted values
ggplot(
  dat_diag_rq2_wb,
  aes(x = fitted, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs. Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted Values",
    y = "Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# 4. Outliers
# Calculate standardized residuals
std_res_wb <- rstandard(model_rq2_wb_mod)

# Count observations with absolute standardized residuals above 3
sum(abs(std_res_wb) > 3)

# Identify unusual observations
which(abs(std_res_wb) > 3)


# 5. Influential Observations
# Calculate Cook's distance
cd_wb <- cooks.distance(model_rq2_wb_mod)

# Plot Cook's distance
plot(
  cd_wb,
  type = "h",
  main = "Cook's Distance: Well-being",
  xlab = "Observation",
  ylab = "Cook's Distance"
)

# Display the 10 largest Cook's distances
head(sort(cd_wb, decreasing = TRUE), 10)

# Count observations exceeding the heuristic threshold
sum(cd_wb > 4 / nobs(model_rq2_wb_mod))


# 6. Multicollinearity
# Check variance inflation factors for the base model
car::vif(model_rq2_wb_base)

# Check variance inflation factors for the moderation model
car::vif(model_rq2_wb_mod)




# Sensitivity Analyses
# Identify the three most influential observations
top3_wb <- order(cd_wb, decreasing = TRUE)[
  seq_len(min(3, length(cd_wb)))
]

# Refit the model after excluding the three most influential cases
model_wb_sens_a <- update(
  model_rq2_wb_mod,
  data = model.frame(model_rq2_wb_mod)[-top3_wb, , drop = FALSE]
)

# Identify observations exceeding Cook's distance threshold
keep_wb <- cd_wb <= 4 / nobs(model_rq2_wb_mod)

# Refit the model after excluding observations above the threshold
model_wb_sens_b <- update(
  model_rq2_wb_mod,
  data = model.frame(model_rq2_wb_mod)[keep_wb, , drop = FALSE]
)

# Compare regression coefficients across models
cbind(
  full = coef(model_rq2_wb_mod),
  without_top3 = coef(model_wb_sens_a),
  without_4n = coef(model_wb_sens_b)
)

# Compare confidence intervals
confint(model_rq2_wb_mod)
confint(model_wb_sens_a)
confint(model_wb_sens_b)

```

#### Missing data report based on complete-case analysis

```{r}
# select all variables
dat_missing_rq2_wb <- dat_rq2_wb %>%
  filter(wave == "K9") %>%
  mutate(
    complete_rq2 = complete.cases(
      wellbeing, wellbeing_K7, K7_ResilFriends,
      K9_orientation, sex, ses
    )
  )

# summarize
dat_missing_rq2_wb %>%
  summarise(
    N_total = n(),
    missing_wb_K9 = sum(is.na(wellbeing)),
    missing_wb_K7 = sum(is.na(wellbeing_K7)),
    missing_peer = sum(is.na(K7_ResilFriends)),
    missing_orientation = sum(is.na(K9_orientation)),
    missing_sex = sum(is.na(sex)),
    missing_ses = sum(is.na(ses)),
    N_complete = sum(complete_rq2),
    N_incomplete = sum(!complete_rq2),
    percent_complete = round(mean(complete_rq2) * 100, 1)
  )

# show included and excluded participants separate per variable
dat_missing_rq2_wb %>%
  group_by(K9_orientation, complete_rq2) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    mean_int_K7 = mean(wellbeing_K7, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_peer = mean(K7_ResilFriends, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_ses = mean(ses, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_female = mean(sex == "Female", na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# H2b: internalizing symptoms

```{r}
# K7 Internalizing als Baseline-Wert pro Person
baseline_int <- dat %>%
  filter(wave == "K7") %>%
  select(person_id, internalizing_K7 = internalizing)
# überprüfen, dass jede Person nur eine Zeile braucht
baseline_int %>% count(person_id) %>% filter(n > 1)

# an Long-Datensatz anhängen
dat_rq2_int <- dat %>%
  left_join(baseline_int, by = "person_id")

nrow(dat_rq2_int)


# Nur vollständige Fälle für dieses Modell
dat_rq2_int_k9 <- dat_rq2_int %>%
  filter(wave == "K9") %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(internalizing),
    !is.na(internalizing_K7),
    !is.na(K7_ResilFriends),
    !is.na(K9_orientation),
    !is.na(sex),
    !is.na(ses))%>%
  mutate(ses_c = (ses - mean(ses[!duplicated(person_id)])) / 10)
  

# Internalizing Symptoms und Peersupport zentrieren ### -> vielleicht in ein separaten Chunk tun
dat_rq2_int_k9 <- dat_rq2_int_k9 %>%
  mutate(
    peer_c = K7_ResilFriends - mean(K7_ResilFriends),
    int_K7_c = internalizing_K7 - mean(internalizing_K7)
  )

# Stichprobe kontrollieren
nrow(dat_rq2_int_k9)
table(dat_rq2_int_k9$K9_orientation)


# Modell 1: Haupteffekt von Peer Support
model_rq2_int_base <- lm(
  internalizing ~ int_K7_c + peer_c + K9_orientation + sex + ses_c,
  data = dat_rq2_int_k9
)

summary(model_rq2_int_base)


# Modell 2: Moderation durch sexuelle Orientierung

model_rq2_int_mod <- lm(
  internalizing ~ int_K7_c + peer_c * K9_orientation + sex + ses_c,
  data = dat_rq2_int_k9
)

summary(model_rq2_int_mod)

# COhens D erhalten
install.packages("parameters"); library(parameters)
parameters::standardize_parameters(model_rq2_int_mod, method = "refit")

# Konfidenzintervalle
emtrends(
  model_rq2_int_mod,
  ~ K9_orientation,
  var = "peer_c"
) |>
  summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
```

```{r}
# 2. Linearity

# Check linearity of continuous predictors in the base model
car::crPlots(

)


# 3. Homoscedasticity

# Extract fitted values and residuals from the moderation model

) +

  ) +

# Calculate standardized residuals
std_res_int <- rstandard(model_rq2_int_mod)

which(abs(std_res_int) > 3)


# 5. Influential Observations

# Calculate Cook's distance
cd_int <- cooks.distance(model_rq2_int_mod)

# Plot Cook's distance
plot(
  cd_int,
  type = "h",
  main = "Cook's Distance: Internalizing Symptoms",     # EINE PERSON STICHT SEHR STARK HERAUS.. ÜBERPRÜFEN, SENSITIVITÄTSANALYSE?
  xlab = "Observation",
  ylab = "Cook's Distance"
)

# Display the 10 largest Cook's distances
head(sort(cd_int, decreasing = TRUE), 10)

# 7. Multicollinearity

car::vif(model_rq2_int_base)

# Sensitivity Analyses
# Identify the three most influential observations

  seq_len(min(3, length(cd_int)))
]

# Refit the model after excluding the three most influential cases

  model_rq2_int_mod,
  data = model.frame(model_rq2_int_mod)[-top3_int, , drop = FALSE]
)

# Identify observations exceeding Cook's distance threshold

# Count excluded observations
sum(!keep_int)

# Calculate the percentage of excluded observations
round(mean(!keep_int) * 100, 1)

# Refit the model after excluding observations above the threshold
model_int_sens_b <- update(
  model_rq2_int_mod,
  data = model.frame(model_rq2_int_mod)[keep_int, , drop = FALSE]
)

# Compare regression coefficients across models -> # grosse Änderung aufgrund eines Falls
cbind(

)
```
